To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adenovirus-based transfection particles are formed by a combination of a replication-defective adenovirus, poly(L-lysines), asialoglycoproteins and a plasmid encoding a reporter gene and that the adenovirus component of this complex is essential for the enhanced transfection efficiency of the plasmids.
a ligand-poly(L-lysin)-modified adenovirus particle was constructed and that it was found to be a potent transgene delivery vehicle.
a replication-defective adenovirus can be used as a vector for the efficient delivery of plasmid DNA to cells that express asialoglycoproteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of adenovirus-based gene transfer vectors that combine the advantages of both viral and non-viral vectors.
the development of a non-viral vector for gene therapy applications that combines the advantages of adenovirus-mediated gene transfer with ligand-mediated DNA complexation.
the development of adenovirus-based transfection systems where the plasmids and adenovirus components are contained within a complex structure that can be readily purified and stored.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adenovirus-based gene delivery complex is an effective vehicle for plasmid transfection in vitro and in vivo.
the adenovirus-based gene transfer system is a promising alternative to viral gene transfer systems.
adenovirus is a useful tool to enhance gene transfer by ligand-mediated endocytotic mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adenovirus-based transfection particle is an effective means for delivering plasmid DNA to target cells, and the adenovirus is a key structural element in this process.
the adenovirus-based gene delivery system represents an efficient and safe means for the delivery of plasmid DNA to target cells.

the use of a non-infectious virus as a carrier for plasmid-based transfection particles can be a useful strategy for the delivery of plasmid transgenes to cells that express specific cell surface receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

adenoviral particles modified with poly(L-Lysine) can be used to form a biomolecular complex with a plasmid and a polycation-ligation complex that can mediate efficient gene transfer to cells that express a specific ligand receptor.
a non-infectious adenovirus-based vector can be used to enhance the level of transfection in a receptor-mediated manner.
adenovirus-based complexes can be used as a gene transfer system for in vivo and in vivo applications.
